standard.title: Planning and budgeting
standard.description: processes that individuals and/or businesses use to plan and budget to achieve short-term and long-term financial objectives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand consumer rights and financial responsibilities (AC9HE7K05). They understand income sources and the reasons individuals work (AC9HE7K04). They have context from AC9HE8K04 on how the taxation system affects individual financial decisions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain processes that individuals and/or businesses use to plan and budget to achieve short-term and long-term financial objectives.

nodes.label: Personal financial objectives and planning tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify ways that short-term and long-term personal financial objectives can be achieved, including through developing a budget and savings plan.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one short-term and one long-term personal financial objective and explain one process (e.g. a budget or savings plan) that could help achieve each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify ways that short-term and long-term personal financial objectives can be achieved, explaining how tools such as a personal budget and savings plan work, and how they can be adapted to different income and expenditure situations.
wider: Investigate how interest rates affect personal saving and borrowing decisions — calculating the effect of compound interest on a savings target over different timeframes
Examine how life stage affects financial planning priorities: comparing the financial objectives and planning tools relevant to a young person starting work versus someone approaching retirement
Research how financial literacy interventions in schools affect long-term financial wellbeing outcomes, and evaluate what financial skills are most important to develop early
nodes.hinge_reason: The personal financial planning node establishes the conceptual frame (short-term vs long-term objectives; planning as a process not a one-off decision) that the business financial planning node builds on. Students who have only encountered budgeting as a static document rather than a dynamic planning process will not connect it to the business tools in the next node.

response_modes.reason: Budget construction is a procedural skill with common errors (confusing income and expenditure categories, conflating savings with surplus). Students benefit from practising with real-number scenarios before the concept is extended to business contexts.

success_criteria: Distinguishes between a short-term and long-term personal financial objective
Explains how a budget or savings plan can be used to work toward a specific financial objective

nodes.label: Business financial records and decision-making
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how financial records — including income statements, balance sheets, budgets and cash flow statements — inform business decision-making.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what one type of business financial record (e.g. an income statement or cash flow statement) shows, and describe one decision a business might make based on that information.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how financial records — income statements, balance sheets, budgets and cash flow statements — each provide different information that informs different types of business decision-making (profitability, solvency, planning, liquidity). Explain how reading these records together gives a more complete picture of financial health.
wider: Investigate how investors and lenders use business financial statements to assess risk before providing capital — examining what each record signals about a business's financial position

Examine a real Australian publicly listed company's annual report, identifying what the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement reveal and any financial risks or opportunities they suggest
Research how accounting standards and audit requirements create trust in financial records — and what happens when financial records are manipulated (e.g. corporate accounting scandals)

response_modes.reason: Students often confuse the four record types (particularly income statement vs balance sheet vs cash flow). Explicit structural comparison — what question does each document answer? what time period does it cover? — prevents conflation and builds transferable financial literacy.

success_criteria: Names at least two types of business financial records and describes the different information each provides
Explains how one type of financial record informs a specific business decision

nodes.label: Business planning processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain business processes used to manage finances and plan in the short and long term, including business plans, borrowing from financial institutions and building savings through interest.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one short-term and one long-term business financial planning process and explain how each helps a business manage its finances toward an objective.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and explain business processes used for short-term and long-term financial planning: devising a business plan, borrowing from financial institutions to fund growth or operations, and building savings through earned interest. Explain how each process serves a different planning horizon or financial need.
wider: Investigate the components of a business plan and why banks and investors require them before providing finance — examining what a business plan signals about financial preparedness and risk
Research how small businesses in Australia access finance through different channels (bank loans, microfinance, crowdfunding, government grants) and the advantages and constraints of each

Examine how a business uses break-even analysis as a planning tool — calculating the volume of sales needed to cover costs and what this means for short-term survival and long-term investment decisions

response_modes.reason: Business planning processes are easiest to understand through concrete cases — a start-up seeking a bank loan, an established business building a reserve fund, a growing business with a multi-year investment plan. Different scenarios illustrate different planning horizons.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Business financial planning processes (business plans, loan assessments, break-even analysis) connect to real decisions students will encounter as entrepreneurs, employees or investors. Wider contexts — including how First Nations community businesses navigate access to capital — add both practical and equity dimensions.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two business processes used for financial planning or management
Explains how one of these processes helps a business work toward a short-term or long-term financial objective

nodes.label: Planning and budgeting — integrated
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how individuals and businesses use planning and budgeting processes to achieve short-term and long-term financial objectives, drawing on appropriate financial records and planning tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how either an individual or a business would use at least two planning or budgeting processes together to work toward a stated financial objective.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how individuals and businesses use a connected set of planning and budgeting processes — combining personal budgets, savings plans, business financial records and business planning tools — to achieve both short-term and long-term financial objectives. Apply to a scenario involving real financial decisions.
wider: Analyse a scenario where short-term and long-term objectives are in tension (e.g. spending now to grow a business versus building financial resilience) and evaluate how planning tools help manage that trade-off

Investigate how financial planning processes differ for a First Nations community-owned enterprise, where objectives include community wellbeing and cultural maintenance alongside financial sustainability
Research financial planning challenges faced by young Australians entering the workforce today (housing affordability, superannuation, study debt) and evaluate which planning tools are most relevant

response_modes.reason: The integration task should require connecting personal financial planning (budget, savings plan) with business financial planning (records, business plan) around a concrete scenario, making explicit that both use similar principles at different scales.

success_criteria: Explains the difference between a short-term and long-term financial objective in a realistic scenario
Identifies and explains at least two planning or budgeting processes an individual or business could use to achieve those objectives
